'''Igor V. Dolgachev''' (born 7 April 1944<ref>{{cite book|last1=Dolgachev|first1=Igor V.|last2=Keum|first2=JongHae|last3=Kondō|first3=Shigeyuki|title=Algebraic geometry: Korea-Japan Conference in honor of Igor Dolgachev's 60th birthday, July 5-9, 2004, Korea Institute for Advanced Study, Seoul, Korea|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1WN9ABvYDSQC&pg=PR7|access-date=20 June 2011|date=2007-01-25|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|isbn=978-0-8218-4201-0|pages=7–}}</ref>) is a Russian–American mathematician specializing in [[algebraic geometry]].  He has been a professor at the [[University of Michigan]] since 1978. He introduced [[Dolgachev surface]]s in 1981.<ref name="DonaldsonSociety1990">{{cite book|last1=Donaldson|first1=Simon K.|author1-link=Simon Donaldson| last2=Society|first2=London Mathematical|title=Geometry of low-dimensional manifolds: proceedings of the Durham Symposium, July 1989|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jY2oBGIzaPIC&pg=PA56|access-date=20 June 2011|year=1990|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=978-0-521-39978-4|pages=56–}}</ref>

Dolgachev completed his [[Ph.D.]] at [[Moscow State University]] in 1970, with thesis ''On the purity of the degeneration locus of families of curves'' written under the supervision of [[Igor Shafarevich]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|7627}}</ref>
